title: Bananas (per lb)

drivers.name: Store closure (Mon)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday; 1/7 of the week's sales lost. No prior closure in history for this product at this store.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 438.2. The store closes Monday, reducing the selling period by 1/7 (~14.3%), which directly reduces expected sales. The price increase to $0.68 (+1.5%) is small and recent data (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) shows no lift at this price—actual sales vs baseline were 1.00 and 0.91, respectively. No promotion or event is scheduled. The classical uplift model suggests no effect, and historical price changes show no consistent lift. The closure is a clear driver. Evidence for price impact is weak and negative in recent weeks. The median multiplier is adjusted downward for the closure. No other drivers are supported by evidence.

PRODUCT: Bananas (per lb) | category Produce | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 0.68 (+1.5% vs regular price 0.67)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 438.2 | 5%-95%: 312.7 - 555.9 | 10%-90%: 346.6 - 529.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-21% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
